milestone: Sequential CPU numeric array map with named callbacks
implementation: ArrayMap typed IR resolves a one-argument numeric callback and preserves array length facts. CPU MLIR lowering uses an ordered scf.for with checked source/destination sizes, tensor extraction, an ordinary callback call, and a fresh logical result. Worker kernel extraction imports synchronous callback/helper graphs with remapped function/value/symbol identities and shares imported definitions. Existing checked invocation ABI adds fault propagation and cooperative loop cancellation. No scheduler, ownership runtime, checked ABI or numeric engine changes.

contract.call: map(values, transform) or values -> map(transform); callback is a named source function.
contract.types: Six numeric input/output element types, all 36 pairs frontend/lowering checked. Literal array input receives callback parameter context; typed arrays match exactly.
contract.length: Same length and private extent identity; output element type follows callback result.
contract.evaluation: Sequential input order, one scalar argument per element; empty input calls no callbacks; no hidden index/collection parameters.
contract.effects: Callback and reachable helpers must be synchronous and have completed numeric scalar signatures at the map boundary. Resumable/error/device operations rejected statically.
contract.failures: First selected callback/helper failure keeps its original location. No partial map result; input remains unchanged; all owners settle.
contract.workers: Map inside workers, direct spawn map, nested worker calls, immutable captures, cached awaits, recovery, admission/cancellation/deadlines and checked allocation failure paths.
contract.parallelism: Spawning a map schedules one sequential map; no implicit per-element parallelism.
contract.remaining: Anonymous functions, closures, general-value arrays/callbacks, expected-error callbacks and GPU/parallel-per-element mapping are not implemented.

qualification.scope: Focused map, arrays, tensor inference, frontend, control-flow, numeric/source/worker, storage and selected Metal regressions; not the full 367-test suite.
coverage: 36 numeric input/output identities frontend checked and lowered; call/pipeline syntax and contextual empty arrays.
All six identity maps preserve random/boundary raw bits including floating zero/subnormal/Inf/NaNs, across eight ARM FP environments.
Strided borrowed inputs unchanged, length preserved, retained mapped output after invocation settlement, allocation-failure sweeps and no partial output.
Mapped float64->float32, float64->uint64, int64->float64 and float32->float64 differential conversion cases reuse independent APFloat/integer oracles, checked metadata and active cancellation.
Direct spawn map and mapping in workers; named synchronous helper graphs, conditional callback bodies, nested map helpers and temporary tensor allocation/reduction inside int64 callback.
1/2/4-worker success, cancellation, deadlines, admission; core allocation positions 1-8 plus generated invocation allocation positions 1-8 with two workers.
Cached awaits, recovery, empty map skips a faulting callback, original Arithmetic source from a callback helper and retained array result ownership.
Both failing element orders keep the earliest callback source; invalid callback diagnostics preserve existing executable.
Callback arity/type/effect rejection, transitively resumable helpers, malformed map references/type/length metadata rejected before lowering.
Debug, optimized, ASan/UBSan and separate TSan execution; sanitized frontend; prior array/tensor/worker/Metal regression coverage.

remaining_gates: Broader collection element/result types and first-class functions
Explicit parallel-per-element mapping and expected-error callback semantics
Runtime array-to-tensor constructors and direct CLI array display
Existing ordinary-recursion restrictions in task-enabled modules
Native distributed design discussion before implementation
